stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether caffeine improves attention. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition drank coffee containing 200 milligrams of caffeine. Participants in the other condition drank decaffeinated coffee that tasted the same. The researchers then recorded the number of targets that each participant correctly detected in a ten-minute computer task.

Researchers collected data from 600 university students. For each one, they recorded conscientiousness score on a personality inventory and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.35.
Researchers collected data from 450 adults. For each one, they recorded optimism score and the number of days of illness in a year. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.30.
Researchers collected data from 250 adults. For each one, they recorded resting heart rate and self-rated anxiety. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.38.

Researchers investigated whether a smiling expression makes cartoons seem funnier. They recruited 90 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a pen between their teeth, which produces a smile. Participants in the other condition held a pen between their lips, which prevents a smile. The researchers then recorded the rating from 1 to 10 that each participant gave to a set of cartoons.

Researchers investigated whether regular aerobic exercise improves memory in older adults. They recruited 100 adults aged 60 to 75 and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition walked briskly for 40 minutes three times a week for six months. Participants in the other condition did gentle stretching for the same amount of time. The researchers then recorded the number of locations that each participant correctly recalled on a spatial memory test.

Researchers collected data from 1,000 students. For each one, they recorded intelligence test score at age 11 and average school grade at age 16. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.60.

Researchers investigated whether praise increases hand raising in class. They recruited 50 second-grade students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were praised by the teacher each time they raised a hand before speaking. Children in the other condition received no special response when they raised a hand. The researchers then recorded the number of times that each child raised a hand during one week.

Researchers investigated whether mindfulness meditation lowers stress. They recruited 84 office workers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition practiced mindfulness meditation for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition listened to an audiobook for twenty minutes a day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded the level of the stress hormone cortisol in a saliva sample from each participant.

Researchers investigated whether agreeing to a small request makes people more likely to agree to a large one. They recruited 120 homeowners and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Homeowners in one condition were first asked to sign a road-safety petition and two weeks later were asked to put a large sign in their garden. Homeowners in the other condition were only asked to put the large sign in their garden. The researchers then recorded the percentage of homeowners in each group who agreed to display the sign.

Researchers collected data from 350 adults. For each one, they recorded the number of stressful life events in the past year and the number of colds in the past year. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.33.

Researchers investigated whether a new drug reduces anxiety. They recruited 150 adults diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition took the new drug every day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition took a placebo pill that looked identical every day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard anxiety questionnaire after eight weeks.

Researchers investigated whether practice quizzes improve memory more than rereading. They recruited 120 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition read a passage once and then took three practice quizzes on it. Participants in the other condition read the same passage four times. The researchers then recorded the percentage of questions that each participant answered correctly on a test one week later. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

columns.label: Mean score on the final test (%)

rows.group: The group that took practice quizzes
The group that reread the passage

stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 500 adults aged 20 to 80. For each one, they recorded age and score on a timed reasoning test. The correlation between the two measures was r = −0.55.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether a night without sleep slows reaction time. They hypothesized that the amount of sleep would affect reaction time.

**Participants.** The sample was 60 adult volunteers, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition stayed awake all night in the laboratory. Participants in the other condition slept for eight hours in the laboratory. The researchers recorded the average time in milliseconds that each participant took to press a button when a light appeared.

**Results.** The group that stayed awake all night: mean reaction time (ms) = 412. The group that slept for eight hours: mean reaction time (ms) = 318. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Does heavy social media use harm the well-being of teenagers?**

**Source A.** A survey of 1,200 teenagers found a correlation of r = +0.28 between hours of social media use per day and scores on a depression questionnaire. Teenagers who reported feeling lonely tended both to use social media more and to have higher depression scores.

**Source B.** In an experiment, 140 university students were randomly assigned either to limit social media use to 30 minutes a day for three weeks or to continue as usual. At the end, the limited group had a mean loneliness score of 38 and the usual-use group a mean of 45 (p = 0.03).

**Source C.** Researchers interviewed 40 teenagers about their experiences online. Many described feeling worse about themselves after viewing images of peers who seemed more attractive or popular; others described feeling supported by online friends who shared their interests.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the organizing of information into broad categories divided into narrower ones?

options.why: A mnemonic device is a memory aid that uses vivid images or organizing tricks.
Massed practice is study that is crammed into one long session.
The method of loci is the mnemonic of imagining items placed at locations along a familiar route.
Correct. A hierarchy is the organizing of information into broad categories divided into narrower ones.

questions.explanation: A hierarchy is the organizing of information into broad categories divided into narrower ones.

questions.stem: All of the subjects in this study were drawn from one group: 80 university students. What does this most limit?

options.text: Whether the study had a control group
options.why: The study had a comparison condition.

options.text: Whether the dependent variable was operationally defined
options.why: The measure was clearly defined.

options.text: Whether a cause-and-effect conclusion can be drawn
options.why: Random assignment, not the sample, allows the causal conclusion.

options.text: How far the findings can be generalized to other populations
options.why: Correct. A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

questions.explanation: A sample that does not represent the wider population limits generalizability.

questions.stem: A theory holds that joy and interest encourage people to explore, be creative and form new friendships, which strengthens them for the future. Which theory is this?

options.why: Universal emotions is the basic emotions, such as happiness, sadness, fear and anger, whose facial expressions are recognized across cultures.
Cognitive appraisal is the interpretation of a situation, which shapes the emotion a person feels.
Correct. The broaden-and-build theory is the theory that positive emotions widen a person's awareness and help build lasting skills and resources.
The facial-feedback hypothesis is the idea that the expression on a person's face can influence the emotion the person feels.

questions.explanation: The broaden-and-build theory is the theory that positive emotions widen a person's awareness and help build lasting skills and resources.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes disorganized attachment?

options.text: The insecure attachment style in which a child shows confused, contradictory behavior toward the caregiver
options.why: Correct. This is what disorganized attachment means.

options.text: The distress that infants show when a familiar caregiver leaves, which peaks around 13 months
options.why: That describes separation anxiety.

options.text: The comfort from physical touch that Harlow showed is more important to attachment than feeding
options.why: That describes contact comfort.

options.text: The attachment style in which a child uses the caregiver as a safe base, is upset when the caregiver leaves and is comforted on return
options.why: That describes secure attachment.

questions.explanation: Disorganized attachment is the insecure attachment style in which a child shows confused, contradictory behavior toward the caregiver.

questions.stem: After two neurons fire together repeatedly, the synapse between them becomes more efficient. What is this process called?

options.why: The central executive is the part of working memory that directs attention and coordinates the other parts.
The visuospatial sketchpad is the part of working memory that briefly holds images and spatial information.
Correct. Long-term potentiation is the strengthening of the connections between neurons after repeated activation, which is the biological basis of memory.
The phonological loop is the part of working memory that briefly holds spoken and written words.

questions.explanation: Long-term potentiation is the strengthening of the connections between neurons after repeated activation, which is the biological basis of memory.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the level of performance typical of a certain chronological age on an intelligence test?

options.why: The intelligence quotient is originally, mental age divided by chronological age and multiplied by 100.
The Flynn effect is the steady rise in average intelligence test scores over the generations.
General intelligence is the single underlying mental ability that Spearman believed affects performance on all mental tasks.
Correct. Mental age is the level of performance typical of a certain chronological age on an intelligence test.

questions.explanation: Mental age is the level of performance typical of a certain chronological age on an intelligence test.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the structure that forms new explicit memories of facts and events?

options.why: Correct. The hippocampus is the structure that forms new explicit memories of facts and events.
The hypothalamus is the structure that regulates hunger, thirst, body temperature and sexual behavior and controls the pituitary gland.
The corpus callosum is the band of fibers that connects the two hemispheres of the brain.
The amygdala is the structure that processes fear and aggression.

questions.explanation: The hippocampus is the structure that forms new explicit memories of facts and events.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = −0.55. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

options.text: The relationship with the positive sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: A doctor records a newborn as female on the basis of anatomy and chromosomes. The doctor is recording which of the following?

options.why: Sexual orientation is the direction of a person's enduring sexual attraction.
Gender identity is a person's own sense of being male, female, neither or some combination.
Correct. Sex is the biological characteristics, such as chromosomes and anatomy, by which people are classified as male, female or intersex.
A gender role is the set of behaviors that a culture expects of men or of women.

questions.explanation: Sex is the biological characteristics, such as chromosomes and anatomy, by which people are classified as male, female or intersex.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the inability to remember where, when or how a piece of information was learned?

options.why: Imagination inflation is the increased confidence that an event happened after repeatedly imagining it.
The misinformation effect is the distortion of a memory by misleading information received after the event.
Correct. Source amnesia is the inability to remember where, when or how a piece of information was learned.
Constructive memory is the building of a memory at retrieval from stored pieces, expectations and later information.

questions.explanation: Source amnesia is the inability to remember where, when or how a piece of information was learned.

questions.stem: Rats that wandered a maze with no reward for ten days ran it almost perfectly as soon as food was placed at the end. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Observational learning is learning by watching others and imitating them.
A cognitive map is a mental picture of the layout of one's surroundings.
Vicarious conditioning is learning from seeing the consequences of another person's behavior.
Correct. Latent learning is learning that takes place without reinforcement and is not shown until there is a reason to show it.

questions.explanation: Latent learning is learning that takes place without reinforcement and is not shown until there is a reason to show it.

questions.stem: After taking a drug, a person sees vivid images that are not there and loses track of time. Which type of drug is this most likely to be?

options.why: Correct. A hallucinogen is a drug, such as marijuana, that distorts perception and can cause sensory experiences without sensory input.
A stimulant is a drug, such as caffeine or cocaine, that speeds up neural activity and body functions.
An opioid is a drug, such as heroin, that relieves pain by acting on endorphin receptors and is highly addictive.
A depressant is a drug, such as alcohol, that slows neural activity and body functions.

questions.explanation: A hallucinogen is a drug, such as marijuana, that distorts perception and can cause sensory experiences without sensory input.

questions.stem: Can the researchers conclude that optimism score causes a change in the number of days of illness in a year?

options.text: Yes, because the correlation is not zero
options.why: Any nonzero correlation still leaves the cause unknown.

options.text: No, because a correlation does not show cause and effect
options.why: Correct. Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

options.text: No, because correlations can only be calculated in experiments
options.why: Correlations are calculated in non-experimental studies.

options.text: Yes, because the sample was large
options.why: A large sample does not turn a correlation into evidence of causation.

questions.explanation: Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

questions.stem: A teenager asks to borrow 100 dollars, is refused, and then asks for 20 dollars, which she receives. Which technique is this?

options.why: A social norm is a rule for accepted and expected behavior in a group.
Correct. The door-in-the-face technique is the strategy of making a large request that will be refused so that a smaller request is more likely to be accepted.
Informational social influence is the influence that comes from a person's willingness to accept others' views as evidence about reality.
Normative social influence is the influence that comes from a person's desire to gain approval or avoid rejection.

questions.explanation: The door-in-the-face technique is the strategy of making a large request that will be refused so that a smaller request is more likely to be accepted.

questions.stem: In a conformity study, six of the seven people at the table are actors who give wrong answers on purpose. Each actor is which of the following?

options.why: Correct. A confederate is a person who seems to be a participant but is secretly working for the researcher.
Informed assent is the agreement of a minor to take part in a study, given in addition to a parent's consent.
Confidentiality is the keeping private of participants' identities and data.
An institutional review board is the committee that reviews research plans to make sure participants are treated ethically.

questions.explanation: A confederate is a person who seems to be a participant but is secretly working for the researcher.

questions.stem: Severe stress early in life switches off a gene in a rat pup, even though the pup's DNA sequence is unchanged. Which field studies this kind of effect?

options.why: Correct. Epigenetics is the study of how the environment changes whether genes are expressed without changing the DNA itself.
An adoption study is research that compares adopted children with their biological and adoptive relatives.
Eugenics is the discredited movement that misused ideas about heredity to argue for selective breeding of humans.
Nurture is the influence of environmental factors, such as upbringing and experience, on behavior and mental processes.

questions.explanation: Epigenetics is the study of how the environment changes whether genes are expressed without changing the DNA itself.

questions.stem: The word 'unkindly' has three meaningful parts: un, kind and ly. Each of these parts is which of the following?

options.why: A phoneme is the smallest distinctive unit of sound in a language.
Syntax is the rules for ordering words into sentences.
Grammar is the whole system of rules in a language that lets people communicate.
Correct. A morpheme is the smallest unit of language that carries meaning.

questions.explanation: A morpheme is the smallest unit of language that carries meaning.

questions.stem: A logo is made of three separate curved lines, but people see a complete circle. Which Gestalt principle explains this?

options.why: Figure and ground is the Gestalt principle that we organize a scene into an object that stands out and its background.
Similarity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that look alike.
Correct. Closure is the Gestalt principle that we fill in gaps to see a complete, whole object.
Proximity is the Gestalt principle that we group together objects that are near each other.

questions.explanation: Closure is the Gestalt principle that we fill in gaps to see a complete, whole object.

questions.stem: What does the correlation show?

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with higher values of the second
options.why: Correct. A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

options.text: Higher values of the first measure tend to go with lower values of the second
options.why: That would be a negative correlation.

options.text: The first measure causes the second
options.why: A correlation does not show cause and effect.
A correlation of zero would show no relationship.

questions.explanation: A positive correlation means the two measures tend to move in the same direction.

questions.stem: When a crisis hits, Maria phones her friends, checks on her children and organizes the neighbors to help one another. Which response to stress is this?

options.why: Correct. The tend-and-befriend response is the response to stress of caring for others and seeking social support.
Eustress is the positive, motivating stress that comes from a challenge.
The fight-or-flight response is the response to stress in which the sympathetic nervous system prepares the body to attack or escape.
Health psychology is the field that studies how behavior, thoughts and emotions affect physical health and illness.

questions.explanation: The tend-and-befriend response is the response to stress of caring for others and seeking social support.

questions.stem: Jamal reads a phone number and can hold it in mind for about twenty seconds before it fades. Which memory store is he using?

options.why: Echoic memory is the sensory memory of a sound, which lasts three or four seconds.
Correct. Short-term memory is the memory store that briefly holds a few items, about seven, before they are stored or forgotten.
Iconic memory is the brief sensory memory of a visual image, which lasts a few tenths of a second.
Working memory is the active processing of information held in mind, combining new input with knowledge from long-term memory.

questions.explanation: Short-term memory is the memory store that briefly holds a few items, about seven, before they are stored or forgotten.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the improved performance on simple or well-learned tasks in the presence of others?

options.why: Groupthink is the kind of thinking in which the desire for agreement in a group overrides a realistic evaluation of alternatives.
Diffusion of responsibility is the reduced sense of personal duty to act when other people are present.
Group polarization is the strengthening of a group's existing opinions after the members discuss them.
Correct. Social facilitation is the improved performance on simple or well-learned tasks in the presence of others.

questions.explanation: Social facilitation is the improved performance on simple or well-learned tasks in the presence of others.

questions.stem: After ten years without cycling, Raj gets on a bicycle and rides without thinking about it. Which kind of memory is this?

options.why: Semantic memory is the explicit memory of facts and general knowledge.
Correct. Procedural memory is the implicit memory of how to perform skills and actions.
Prospective memory is the memory to carry out a planned action in the future.
Episodic memory is the explicit memory of personally experienced events.

questions.explanation: Procedural memory is the implicit memory of how to perform skills and actions.

questions.stem: In the middle of laughing at a joke, Viktor suddenly falls asleep. Which sleep disorder does he most likely have?

options.why: Somnambulism is sleepwalking, which occurs during deep NREM sleep.
REM sleep behavior disorder is a sleep disorder in which the normal paralysis of REM sleep is missing, so the person acts out dreams.
Sleep apnea is a sleep disorder in which breathing repeatedly stops during sleep, causing brief awakenings.
Correct. Narcolepsy is a sleep disorder with sudden, uncontrollable attacks of sleep, often straight into REM sleep.

questions.explanation: Narcolepsy is a sleep disorder with sudden, uncontrollable attacks of sleep, often straight into REM sleep.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: The two groups differed in amusement at the end of the study
options.why: That is the dependent variable, the result being measured.

options.text: One group differed from the other in the facial expression produced by holding a pen
options.why: That is the independent variable itself.

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

options.text: The group holding the pen between the teeth saw the cartoons in color, and the other group saw them in black and white
options.why: Correct. It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.explanation: It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.stem: To remember the term 'hippocampus', Sol links it to a hippo on a campus who never forgets his classes. Which technique is he using?

options.why: Autobiographical memory is the memory of the events of one's own life.
Highly superior autobiographical memory is the rare ability to recall almost every day of one's life in detail.
Maintenance rehearsal is the repeating of information over and over to keep it in short-term memory.
Correct. Elaborative rehearsal is the linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory.

questions.explanation: Elaborative rehearsal is the linking of new information to existing knowledge and meaning to store it in long-term memory.

questions.stem: Ben is tormented by constant worry and feels miserable most of the day. Which criterion for a psychological disorder does this meet?

options.why: The DSM is the American Psychiatric Association's manual for classifying and diagnosing psychological disorders.
The ICD is the World Health Organization's international system for classifying all diseases, including mental disorders.
Correct. Distress is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior causes suffering to the person.
Stigma is the negative attitudes and discrimination directed at people who have a psychological disorder.

questions.explanation: Distress is the criterion for a disorder that the behavior causes suffering to the person.

questions.stem: Students are asked whether each word on a list rhymes with 'cat'. Which level of processing does this task use?

options.why: Correct. Phonemic encoding is the encoding of a word based on its sound.
Structural encoding is the shallow encoding of a word based on its appearance.
Explicit memory is the memory of facts and experiences that a person can consciously recall and state.
Automatic processing is the encoding of information, such as space, time and frequency, without conscious effort.

questions.explanation: Phonemic encoding is the encoding of a word based on its sound.

questions.stem: A crawling infant refuses to cross a sheet of glass over what looks like a steep drop. Which apparatus is being used?

options.why: Imprinting is the process by which some animals form a strong attachment to the first moving object they see.
A critical period is a limited time early in life when certain experiences must occur for normal development.
Gross motor skills is the movements that use large muscles, such as crawling, walking and jumping.
Correct. The visual cliff is the laboratory apparatus with a glass-covered drop that is used to test depth perception in infants.

questions.explanation: The visual cliff is the laboratory apparatus with a glass-covered drop that is used to test depth perception in infants.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the conversion of physical energy, such as light or sound, into neural impulses?

options.why: Sensory adaptation is the reduced sensitivity that follows constant, unchanging stimulation.
Weber's law is the principle that two stimuli must differ by a constant proportion, not a constant amount, to be noticed.
The absolute threshold is the weakest level of a stimulus that a person can detect half of the time.
Correct. Transduction is the conversion of physical energy, such as light or sound, into neural impulses.

questions.explanation: Transduction is the conversion of physical energy, such as light or sound, into neural impulses.

questions.stem: Which group served as the control group?

options.why: Only the comparison group is the control group.

options.text: Neither group, because the study had no comparison condition
options.why: The second condition is the comparison.

options.text: The group that did gentle stretching
options.why: Correct. The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.
This group received the treatment being tested: it is the experimental group.

questions.explanation: The control group is the comparison group that does not receive the treatment being tested.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as unjustified negative behavior toward a group and its members?

options.why: Ethnocentrism is the tendency to judge other cultures by the standards of one's own culture.
Correct. Discrimination is unjustified negative behavior toward a group and its members.
A stereotype is a generalized belief about a group of people.
The just-world phenomenon is the tendency to believe that people get what they deserve.

questions.explanation: Discrimination is unjustified negative behavior toward a group and its members.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the directionality problem in this study?

options.text: It is unclear whether the first measure influences the second or the second influences the first
options.why: Correct. A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

options.text: It is unclear whether the two measures were recorded
options.why: Both measures were recorded.

options.text: It is unclear how many people took part
options.why: The sample size is stated.

options.text: It is unclear whether the correlation is positive or negative
options.why: The sign of r shows the direction of the relationship.

questions.explanation: A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes openness to experience?

options.text: The Big Five trait of being calm and secure rather than anxious and moody
options.why: That describes emotional stability.

options.text: The Big Five trait of being organized, careful and self-disciplined
options.why: That describes conscientiousness.

options.text: The Big Five trait of being sociable, outgoing and energetic
options.why: That describes extraversion.

options.text: The Big Five trait of being imaginative, curious and willing to try new things
options.why: Correct. This is what openness to experience means.

questions.explanation: Openness to experience is the Big Five trait of being imaginative, curious and willing to try new things.

questions.stem: For the past year, Kate has worried constantly about her health, money and family, with tense muscles and poor sleep, and no single cause. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Social anxiety disorder is the disorder in which a person has an intense fear of being judged or embarrassed in social situations.
Correct. Generalized anxiety disorder is the disorder in which a person feels tense and worried most of the time about many things, for at least six months.
Panic disorder is the disorder in which a person has repeated, unexpected episodes of intense fear with physical symptoms such as chest pain.
A specific phobia is the disorder in which a person has an intense, irrational fear of a particular object or situation.

questions.explanation: Generalized anxiety disorder is the disorder in which a person feels tense and worried most of the time about many things, for at least six months.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the operational definition of the dependent variable?

options.text: The number of times that each child raised a hand during one week
options.why: Correct. An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

options.text: The random assignment of each one to a condition
options.why: This is a control procedure, not a definition of a variable.
This is the independent variable.
This names the variable but does not say how it was measured.

questions.explanation: An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

questions.stem: Antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic personality disorders belong to which cluster?

options.why: Cluster C is the group of personality disorders marked by anxious or fearful behavior: avoidant, dependent and obsessive-compulsive.
Correct. Cluster B is the group of personality disorders marked by dramatic, emotional or erratic behavior: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic.
Cluster A is the group of personality disorders marked by odd or eccentric behavior: paranoid, schizoid and schizotypal.
A personality disorder is a lasting, rigid pattern of behavior and inner experience that differs from cultural expectations and impairs functioning.

questions.explanation: Cluster B is the group of personality disorders marked by dramatic, emotional or erratic behavior: antisocial, borderline, histrionic and narcissistic.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the operational definition of the dependent variable?

options.text: The random assignment of each one to a condition
options.why: This is a control procedure, not a definition of a variable.
This names the variable but does not say how it was measured.
This is the independent variable.

options.text: The level of the stress hormone cortisol in a saliva sample from each participant
options.why: Correct. An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

questions.explanation: An operational definition states exactly how a variable is measured.

questions.stem: Students are 90 percent sure of answers that turn out to be right only 60 percent of the time. Which tendency is this?

options.why: Experimenter bias is the influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study.
Correct. Overconfidence is the tendency to be more certain than correct about one's own judgments.
Social desirability bias is the tendency of participants to answer in a way that makes them look good.
Self-report bias is the inaccuracy that arises when people describe their own behavior or feelings.

questions.explanation: Overconfidence is the tendency to be more certain than correct about one's own judgments.

questions.stem: The group that first signed the petition agreed more often. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: Whether a small request came first caused the difference in compliance with a large request
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

options.text: Whether a small request came first and compliance with a large request are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as in classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning?

options.why: The conditioned response is in classical conditioning, the learned response to a previously neutral stimulus.
Correct. The unconditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning.
The conditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the originally neutral stimulus that triggers a response after being paired with another stimulus.
The unconditioned response is in classical conditioning, the natural, unlearned response to a stimulus.

questions.explanation: The unconditioned stimulus is in classical conditioning, the stimulus that triggers a response naturally, without learning.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a culture's preferred timing for life events such as marriage, parenthood and retirement?

options.why: Correct. The social clock is a culture's preferred timing for life events such as marriage, parenthood and retirement.
Adverse childhood experiences is the stressful or traumatic events in childhood, such as abuse or neglect, that raise the risk of later problems.
Parallel play is the play of young children who play side by side without interacting.
The personal fable is the belief of adolescents that they are unique and that bad things will not happen to them.

questions.explanation: The social clock is a culture's preferred timing for life events such as marriage, parenthood and retirement.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the formal operational stage?

options.text: Piaget's stage from about age 7 to 11, in which children think logically about real objects and events
options.why: That describes the concrete operational stage.

options.text: Piaget's stage from about age 2 to 7, in which children use words and images but cannot yet reason logically
options.why: That describes the preoperational stage.

options.text: Piaget's stage from birth to about age 2, in which infants know the world through senses and actions
options.why: That describes the sensorimotor stage.

options.text: Piaget's stage from about age 12 on, in which people can reason about abstract and hypothetical ideas
options.why: Correct. This is what the formal operational stage means.

questions.explanation: The formal operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 12 on, in which people can reason about abstract and hypothetical ideas.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a cross-sectional study?

options.text: The developmental question of how heredity and experience together shape a person
options.why: That describes nature and nurture.

options.text: The view that development is a gradual, steady process, like a ramp
options.why: That describes continuous development.

options.text: Research that compares people of different ages at one point in time
options.why: Correct. This is what a cross-sectional study means.

options.text: Research that follows the same people and retests them over a long period
options.why: That describes a longitudinal study.

questions.explanation: A cross-sectional study is research that compares people of different ages at one point in time.

questions.stem: Dana must choose between two universities, both of which she would love to attend. Which kind of conflict is this?

options.why: Correct. An approach-approach conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two attractive options.
Extrinsic motivation is the desire to do something to gain a reward or avoid a punishment.
An avoidance-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two unattractive options.
An approach-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which one option has both attractive and unattractive features.

questions.explanation: An approach-approach conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two attractive options.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the inability to form new memories after an injury or illness?

options.why: Correct. Anterograde amnesia is the inability to form new memories after an injury or illness.
Alzheimer's disease is a progressive brain disease that destroys memory and then other mental abilities.
Retrograde amnesia is the loss of memories from before an injury or illness.
Infantile amnesia is the inability of adults to remember events from the first few years of life.

questions.explanation: Anterograde amnesia is the inability to form new memories after an injury or illness.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.why: Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.
This is the statistic, not a variable.

options.text: The number of stressful life events in the past year
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.

options.text: The number of colds in the past year
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: Receptors in Tia's fingertip detect a pinprick, and a signal travels toward her spinal cord. Which cells carry this incoming signal?

options.why: Correct. Sensory neurons is the neurons that carry incoming information from the sense receptors to the brain and spinal cord.
Motor neurons is the neurons that carry outgoing information from the brain and spinal cord to the muscles and glands.
Glial cells is the cells that support, nourish, insulate and protect neurons.
The reflex arc is the simple automatic pathway in which the spinal cord produces a response before the brain is aware of the stimulus.

questions.explanation: Sensory neurons is the neurons that carry incoming information from the sense receptors to the brain and spinal cord.

questions.stem: Four studies of child development report these correlation coefficients: +0.70, −0.86, +0.52, −0.93. Which coefficient shows the weakest relationship?

options.why: +0.70 is farther from zero.
Correct. Strength is the distance from zero, whatever the sign; +0.52 is closest to zero.
−0.86 is farther from zero.
−0.93 is farther from zero.

questions.explanation: The sign of a correlation shows its direction; its distance from zero shows its strength. +0.52 is closest to zero.

questions.stem: After months of use, Dan needs twice as much of a drug to feel the effect that one dose used to give him. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Withdrawal is the unpleasant physical and psychological symptoms that follow stopping an addictive drug.
Correct. Tolerance is the need for larger doses of a drug to get the same effect after repeated use.
An antagonist is a drug that decreases the action of a neurotransmitter, for example by blocking its receptors.
A reuptake inhibitor is a drug that keeps a neurotransmitter in the synapse longer by blocking its reabsorption.

questions.explanation: Tolerance is the need for larger doses of a drug to get the same effect after repeated use.

questions.stem: After getting food poisoning from fish, Carl feels sick at the smell of fish for years. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Counterconditioning is the replacing of an unwanted response to a stimulus with a new response, by pairing the stimulus with something pleasant.
Habituation is the decrease in response to a stimulus that is presented over and over.
One-trial conditioning is learning that happens after a single pairing of two stimuli.
Correct. A taste aversion is a learned dislike of a food that was followed by illness.

questions.explanation: A taste aversion is a learned dislike of a food that was followed by illness.

questions.stem: A previously healthy student suddenly develops hallucinations after a period of intense stress and later recovers well. Which pattern of onset is this?

options.why: A positive symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that adds an inappropriate behavior or experience, such as hallucinations.
A negative symptom is a symptom of schizophrenia that takes away a normal behavior, such as emotional expression or motivation.
Correct. An acute onset is the sudden appearance of schizophrenia, often after stress, from which recovery is more likely.
A chronic course is the slow, gradual development of schizophrenia, from which recovery is less likely.

questions.explanation: An acute onset is the sudden appearance of schizophrenia, often after stress, from which recovery is more likely.

questions.stem: Fans rate players on their own team as more skilled and more honest than equally good players on other teams. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Confirmation bias is the tendency to search for and favor information that supports what one already believes.
Correct. In-group bias is the tendency to favor the members of one's own group.
Out-group homogeneity bias is the tendency to see the members of other groups as all alike.
Belief perseverance is the tendency to hold on to a belief even after the evidence for it has been discredited.

questions.explanation: In-group bias is the tendency to favor the members of one's own group.

questions.stem: After flying across eight time zones, Kofi is wide awake at 3 a.m. and exhausted at noon. Jet lag is a disruption of which of the following?

options.why: REM sleep is the sleep stage with rapid eye movements, vivid dreams, an active brain and relaxed muscles.
REM rebound is the tendency to have more REM sleep after being deprived of it.
Correct. The circadian rhythm is the body's roughly 24-hour cycle of wakefulness and sleep.
NREM stage 1 is the brief, light first stage of sleep, in which a person may have hypnagogic sensations such as falling.

questions.explanation: The circadian rhythm is the body's roughly 24-hour cycle of wakefulness and sleep.

questions.stem: A theory explains how we hear high-pitched sounds by saying that they stimulate a particular location on the cochlea. Which theory is this?

options.why: Sound localization is the ability to tell where a sound comes from, using differences in timing and loudness between the two ears.
Conduction deafness is hearing loss caused by damage to the eardrum or the bones of the middle ear.
Correct. Place theory is the theory that we hear different pitches because different sound waves trigger different places on the cochlea's membrane.
Volley theory is the theory that groups of neurons take turns firing so that together they match high sound frequencies.

questions.explanation: Place theory is the theory that we hear different pitches because different sound waves trigger different places on the cochlea's membrane.

questions.stem: Several times a week, Ron eats far more than he intends, feels ashamed afterward, but does not vomit or fast. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by inattention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness.
A specific learning disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by persistent difficulty in reading, writing or math despite normal intelligence.
Autism spectrum disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by difficulties with social communication and by repetitive behaviors or narrow interests.
Correct. Binge-eating disorder is the eating disorder in which a person repeatedly eats very large amounts and feels distress, without purging afterward.

questions.explanation: Binge-eating disorder is the eating disorder in which a person repeatedly eats very large amounts and feels distress, without purging afterward.

questions.stem: Before taking part, each participant was told what the study would involve and what the risks were, and then agreed to take part. Which ethical guideline does this meet?

options.why: Confidentiality is keeping participants' data private.
Correct. Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.
That is a research procedure, not an ethical guideline.
Debriefing happens after the study.

questions.explanation: Participants must agree to take part after being told what the study involves.

questions.stem: After spinning on a ride, Zoe feels dizzy because the fluid in her inner ear is still moving. Which sense is affected?

options.why: Phantom limb sensation is the feeling of pain or touch in a limb that has been amputated.
Correct. The vestibular sense is the sense of balance and head position, based on the semicircular canals of the inner ear.
Kinesthesis is the sense of the position and movement of body parts, based on receptors in muscles and joints.
The gate control theory is the theory that the spinal cord has a gate that can block pain signals or let them pass to the brain.

questions.explanation: The vestibular sense is the sense of balance and head position, based on the semicircular canals of the inner ear.

questions.stem: A researcher reports that the difference between two groups would occur by chance less than 5 times in 100. Which term describes this result?

options.why: Effect size is the measure of how large the difference or relationship found in a study is.
The placebo effect is an improvement that results from a person's expectation of a treatment rather than from the treatment itself.
The experimental group is the group in an experiment that receives the treatment being tested.
Correct. Statistical significance is the conclusion that a result is unlikely to have occurred by chance, usually when p is below 0.05.

questions.explanation: Statistical significance is the conclusion that a result is unlikely to have occurred by chance, usually when p is below 0.05.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the habit of explaining bad events as lasting, affecting everything and caused by oneself?

options.why: An optimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as temporary, specific and caused by outside factors.
Correct. A pessimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as lasting, affecting everything and caused by oneself.
Relative deprivation is the feeling of being worse off than the people one compares oneself with.
The fundamental attribution error is the tendency, when judging other people's behavior, to overestimate personal traits and underestimate the situation.

questions.explanation: A pessimistic explanatory style is the habit of explaining bad events as lasting, affecting everything and caused by oneself.

questions.stem: Scores on a university entrance test correlate strongly with students' later grades. Which quality does the test have?

options.why: Correct. Predictive validity is the extent to which test scores forecast the future performance they are meant to predict.
Standardization is the giving and scoring of a test in the same way for everyone, and the comparison of scores with a pretested group.
Test-retest reliability is the consistency of scores when the same people take the same test twice.
Construct validity is the extent to which a test measures the concept it claims to measure.

questions.explanation: Predictive validity is the extent to which test scores forecast the future performance they are meant to predict.

questions.stem: Which term refers to any loss of the ability to produce or understand language after brain damage?

options.why: Broca's area is the area in the left frontal lobe that controls speech production.
Correct. Aphasia is an impairment of language caused by brain damage.
Hemispheric specialization is the tendency for each side of the brain to handle certain functions, such as language in the left hemisphere.
Wernicke's area is the area in the left temporal lobe that controls language comprehension.

questions.explanation: Aphasia is an impairment of language caused by brain damage.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an algorithm?

options.text: A step-by-step procedure that guarantees a solution
options.why: Correct. This is what an algorithm means.

options.text: The inability to see that an object can be used for something other than its usual purpose
options.why: That describes functional fixedness.

options.text: The mental processes used to plan, organize and carry out goal-directed behavior
options.why: That describes executive functions.

options.text: The tendency to approach a problem in a way that has worked before, even when it no longer works
options.why: That describes a mental set.

questions.explanation: An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure that guarantees a solution.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes courage?

options.text: The category of character strengths that includes creativity, curiosity and love of learning
options.why: That describes wisdom.

options.text: The category of character strengths that includes bravery, honesty and perseverance
options.why: Correct. This is what courage means.

options.text: The category of character strengths that includes teamwork, fairness and leadership
options.why: That describes justice.

options.text: The category of character strengths that includes forgiveness, humility and self-control
options.why: That describes temperance.

questions.explanation: Courage is the category of character strengths that includes bravery, honesty and perseverance.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the cognitive perspective?

options.text: The view that disorders result from social and cultural factors, such as poverty and discrimination
options.why: That describes the sociocultural perspective.

options.text: The view that disorders result from genetic, brain or chemical causes
options.why: That describes the biological perspective.

options.text: The view that disorders result from distorted or irrational ways of thinking
options.why: Correct. This is what the cognitive perspective means.

options.text: The view that disorders result from learned associations and reinforcement
options.why: That describes the behavioral perspective.

questions.explanation: The cognitive perspective is the view that disorders result from distorted or irrational ways of thinking.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the motor cortex?

options.text: The strip at the front of the parietal lobes that registers touch and body sensations
options.why: That describes the somatosensory cortex.

options.text: The lobes at the back of the head, which process visual information
options.why: That describes the occipital lobes.

options.text: The strip at the rear of the frontal lobes that controls voluntary movements
options.why: Correct. This is what the motor cortex means.

options.text: The lobes at the top of the head, which process touch and spatial information
options.why: That describes the parietal lobes.

questions.explanation: The motor cortex is the strip at the rear of the frontal lobes that controls voluntary movements.

questions.stem: A man with strong aggressive urges becomes a successful boxer. Which defense mechanism is this?

options.why: Regression is the defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development.
Reaction formation is the defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses.
Correct. Sublimation is the defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities.
Repression is the defense mechanism of pushing anxiety-arousing thoughts and memories out of awareness.

questions.explanation: Sublimation is the defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities.

questions.stem: Taking a tablet makes Lena's headache go away, so she is more likely to take a tablet next time. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Positive punishment is the weakening of a behavior by adding an unpleasant stimulus after it.
Positive reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by adding a pleasant stimulus after it.
Correct. Negative reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by removing an unpleasant stimulus after it.
Negative punishment is the weakening of a behavior by removing a pleasant stimulus after it.

questions.explanation: Negative reinforcement is the strengthening of a behavior by removing an unpleasant stimulus after it.

questions.stem: A two-year-old insists, 'Me do it!' when getting dressed. Which of Erikson's stages is this?

options.why: Industry versus inferiority is Erikson's stage in elementary school, in which children learn to feel competent or else feel inadequate.
Trust versus mistrust is Erikson's stage in infancy, in which babies learn whether their needs will be met.
Initiative versus guilt is Erikson's stage in the preschool years, in which children learn to start tasks and carry out plans.
Correct. Autonomy versus shame and doubt is Erikson's stage in toddlerhood, in which children learn to do things for themselves.

questions.explanation: Autonomy versus shame and doubt is Erikson's stage in toddlerhood, in which children learn to do things for themselves.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: Why is this study not an experiment?

options.why: Sample size does not determine the research method.

options.text: The researchers did not manipulate a variable or randomly assign anyone to conditions
options.why: Correct. An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.
Experiments also use numerical data.
Experiments also test hypotheses.

questions.explanation: An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a meta-analysis?

options.text: The choosing of treatments on the basis of research, clinical skill and the client's own values
options.why: That describes evidence-based practice.

options.text: The bond of trust and cooperation between therapist and client
options.why: That describes the therapeutic alliance.

options.text: A therapist's openness to learning about a client's culture and awareness of the limits of their own view
options.why: That describes cultural humility.

options.text: A statistical procedure that combines the results of many studies to reach an overall conclusion
options.why: Correct. This is what a meta-analysis means.

questions.explanation: A meta-analysis is a statistical procedure that combines the results of many studies to reach an overall conclusion.

questions.stem: Mr. Hale's house is so full of old newspapers and boxes that he cannot reach his bed, yet he cannot bear to discard anything. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Dissociative identity disorder is the disorder in which a person shows two or more distinct personalities that take control at different times.
A compulsion is a repeated action that a person feels driven to perform to reduce anxiety.
Correct. Hoarding disorder is the disorder in which a person cannot throw away possessions, so that living spaces become cluttered.
Dissociative amnesia is the disorder in which a person cannot remember important personal information, usually after trauma and with no physical cause, sometimes with travel away from home (fugue).

questions.explanation: Hoarding disorder is the disorder in which a person cannot throw away possessions, so that living spaces become cluttered.

questions.stem: A therapist helps a client replace the thought 'I failed one test, so I am stupid' with 'One test does not define me.' Which technique is this?

options.why: Cognitive-behavioral therapy is the therapy that combines changing self-defeating thoughts with changing behavior.
Rational emotive behavior therapy is the confrontational cognitive therapy, developed by Ellis, that actively challenges a client's irrational beliefs.
Correct. Cognitive restructuring is the technique of identifying irrational thoughts and replacing them with more realistic ones.
Dialectical behavior therapy is the therapy that teaches skills for tolerating distress and controlling emotions, often used for borderline personality disorder.

questions.explanation: Cognitive restructuring is the technique of identifying irrational thoughts and replacing them with more realistic ones.

questions.stem: Scores on a test are normally distributed with a mean of 100 and a standard deviation of 20. About what percentage of scores are above 120?

options.why: This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
Correct. 68% lie within one standard deviation, leaving 32% outside, half of which (16%) is above.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.

questions.explanation: 68% lie within one standard deviation, leaving 32% outside, half of which (16%) is above. (80 and 120 are one standard deviation from the mean; 60 and 140 are two.)

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of reaction time

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of reaction time.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Reaction time was defined as the average time in milliseconds that each participant took to press a button when a light appeared.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The group that stayed awake responded more slowly. On average, the value was 412 for the group that stayed awake all night and 318 for the group that slept for eight hours, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 60 adult volunteers from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The group that stayed awake responded more slowly. (412 compared with 318).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that the amount of sleep affects reaction time. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to the amount of sleep. The finding illustrates sleep restores the brain, so sleep loss impairs attention and reaction time.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Does heavy social media use harm the well-being of teenagers?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: Heavy social media use can harm teenagers' well-being, especially when it leads them to compare themselves with others.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, students who limited social media to 30 minutes a day had lower loneliness scores (38) than students who continued as usual (45).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim because the study was an experiment with random assignment, so reducing social media use can be said to have caused the lower loneliness. Less time online leaves more time for face-to-face contact, which supports well-being.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source C, many teenagers said they felt worse about themselves after viewing images of peers who seemed more attractive or popular.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through upward social comparison and relative deprivation: comparing oneself with people who seem better off lowers self-esteem and satisfaction.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
